<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as vinegar

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-vinegar" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-vinegar-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of vinegar, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of vinegar measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 5 groups of vinegar ranged from 510 µg/kg (retail product G (aromatic-alcohol vinegar, Germany origin)) to 600 µg/kg (retail product I (malt vinegar, England origin)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Acosta A, Diaz C, Hardisson A, Gonzalez D · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Levels of Cd, Pb, and Ni in Different Types of Vinegars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-vinegar-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-vinegar-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in vinegar is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in vinegar is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 2 results from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported inorganic arsenic in vinegar, as sold from 3 results in 1 reporting region, with a subgroup median of 1,200 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
